document.title: Write Studio Multi-Vertical Document Creation — Master Implementation Plan and AI Agent Prompt
document.purpose: A complete, actionable source of truth for evolving Write Studio from a UX case-study-focused editor into a multi-vertical, template-driven professional document creation studio.
document.usage: Provide this complete JSON file to the coding agent together with the current repository. The agent must execute phases sequentially and validate each phase before continuing.
document.important_source_note: Any previously uploaded ZIP is a historical source snapshot, not guaranteed to represent the current completed multi-user codebase. The live repository, applied migrations and current production/staging behaviour are the source of truth.

agent_execution_prompt.role: Act as a senior product engineer, UX architect, technical writer, database engineer and QA lead responsible for evolving Write Studio safely.
agent_execution_prompt.mission: Transform Write Studio into a multi-vertical, template-driven document creation studio using one universal editor, one generic private document model, a versioned template engine and a reusable content block registry.
agent_execution_prompt.primary_instruction: Inspect the live repository first. Build on the implemented multi-user foundation. Do not assume old paths, schemas or features still exist. Produce an implementation plan, then execute the approved phases in order. For every phase, explain what you changed, why, the expected result and how it was tested.
operating_rules: Do not begin by rewriting the editor. Audit and reuse the existing working Tiptap engine, toolbar, slash menu, inspector, media handling and renderer wherever appropriate.
Do not create a separate editor for every document type. Use one universal editor configured through template metadata and block availability/recommendations.
Do not hardcode template section headings into editor components. Template structures, prompts, evidence guidance, suggested blocks and validation must be data-driven.
Do not store guidance prompts, UI state or private author notes inside the authored document body unless the user explicitly inserts them as content.
Do not silently modify existing documents when a template or block schema changes. Use versioned, explicit migrations.
Do not weaken authentication, workspace ownership, Row Level Security or private storage policies.
Do not introduce public publishing, public share links, public directories, team collaboration, billing or marketplace functionality in this project scope.
Do not fabricate customer outcomes, release status, technical verification, testimonials, metrics or research findings.
Do not add a block unless it has a schema, editor experience, persistence behaviour, preview renderer, export fallback, validation and accessibility considerations.
Do not mark a phase complete based only on successful compilation. Run its acceptance checks and provide evidence.
If current code already contains a required feature, verify it and reuse or improve it instead of duplicating it.
If an expected capability is not present in the live repository, record the gap and implement it in the correct phase.
Keep design-system tokens as the only source for styling values. Do not introduce hardcoded HEX values into components or design specs; use existing primitive/semantic tokens.
Keep the document editor responsive, keyboard accessible and robust for long documents.
Do not expose private document content in application logs, analytics, URLs, error messages or telemetry.
required_working_method: 1. Inspect repository, current branch, package scripts, routes, editor extensions, data schema, migrations, RLS and storage policies.
2. Produce a current-state inventory and map each requested capability to existing, partial, missing or unsafe implementation.
3. Produce a dependency-aware plan and identify data migration risks before editing.
4. Implement a phase in small, reviewable changes.
5. Run typecheck, lint, build, unit tests, integration tests and relevant E2E tests after each phase.
6. Validate document data integrity and cross-account privacy in staging.
7. Provide a phase report with files changed, migrations, tests, screenshots where applicable, limitations and remaining work.
8. Do not proceed past a failed phase gate without resolving or explicitly documenting the blocker.
agent_execution_prompt.required_final_response: Provide a concise but detailed implementation report: completed phases, files changed, migrations applied, templates delivered, blocks delivered, tests run and results, privacy verification evidence, known limitations, deployment instructions and next recommended iteration.
agent_execution_prompt.phase_completion_rule: A phase is complete only when all phase actions have corresponding implementation or documented deferment, expected deliverables exist, evaluation criteria are evidenced, and exit criteria pass.
agent_execution_prompt.template_implementation_rule: For each template, deliver its definition, sample document, metadata form, section outline, prompts, suggested evidence, block recommendations, validation rules, review checks, preview rendering and relevant export profile.
agent_execution_prompt.block_implementation_rule: For each block, deliver a stable schema/version, insert command, editor renderer, contextual toolbar actions, inspector, validation, preview renderer, export renderer, accessibility behaviour and migration/fallback strategy.
agent_execution_prompt.security_rule: Treat private ownership as a release-blocking invariant. Test with at least two independent authenticated users and unauthenticated access. Never rely on UI hiding as an authorization control.

product_context.current_product: A private multi-user writing and visual composition studio built on Next.js, React, Tiptap/ProseMirror and Supabase.
current_strengths_to_preserve: Existing visual blocks: image grid, comparison, showcase, device mockup, split layout, pull quote, callout and metrics
product_context.new_product_direction: Template-driven professional document creation across multiple verticals, with guided structure, contextual writing guidance, reusable domain blocks and document-specific output profiles.
product_context.positioning: A guided document creation studio: one editor, purpose-built templates, structured content blocks and professional outputs.
product_context.primary_product_outcome: A user should be able to choose a relevant document type, create a useful structure, write and compose the content, review it and export a portable deliverable without assembling several unrelated tools.

locked_product_decisions.editor: One hybrid, document-first editor using Tiptap. Writing remains primary; visual composition is powerful but bounded and responsive.
locked_product_decisions.template_system: One versioned, data-driven template engine. Templates configure structure, prompts, evidence suggestions, blocks, validation and outputs.
locked_product_decisions.document_model: General-purpose private document entity. Do not keep new documents semantically tied to a case-study-only entity.
locked_product_decisions.privacy: All documents, notes, media, previews and exports remain private and owner-scoped.
locked_product_decisions.authentication: Preserve email/password and email OTP authentication with required email verification according to the already implemented account policy.
locked_product_decisions.publishing: No public document publishing or sharing in this scope. Exported copies are created only by the authenticated owner.
locked_product_decisions.editor_engine: Keep current Tiptap/ProseMirror implementation unless audit identifies a concrete blocking limitation.
locked_product_decisions.design_system: Use existing design system and semantic tokens; no hardcoded colour values in product UI.
locked_product_decisions.existing_ux_template: Preserve the existing UX case-study workflow as a first-class template and ensure backward compatibility.

in_scope: PDF, standalone HTML ZIP, Markdown and JSON/asset backup exports
out_of_scope: Public publishing or public document sharing
Public user profiles or public document directories
Automatic AI generation of unverified facts, metrics or customer claims
future_considerations: AI story and technical writing assistance with user consent
Public publishing as a separately designed capability
Specialised template families based on beta demand

goals: Serve multiple professional verticals with a coherent product experience.
Reduce blank-page friction through purpose-built structures and contextual guidance.
Provide domain-aware blocks without maintaining separate editors.
Make documents portable through useful exports.
Preserve existing UX case-study functionality and all private user data.
Make templates and blocks extensible for future verticals.
non_goals: Compete as a general-purpose word processor.
Replace Figma, Framer or Webflow as a general design canvas.
Replace full API platforms or source-code documentation hosting in the initial release.
Require every template to use every section.
Force users to follow framework suggestions.
Introduce AI as a prerequisite for useful writing.

target_audiences.audience: Software engineers, developer advocates, technical writers, platform engineers
Product managers, product designers, business analysts and founders
jobs: Write user stories and acceptance criteria

target_audiences.audience: Product teams, engineering teams, DevRel and customer success
Marketing teams, agencies, growth consultants and customer success
Operations managers, service delivery, HR, support and compliance teams

competitive_inspiration.inspiration: Distraction-free writing, selection-based floating formatting, restrained visible controls.
competitive_inspiration.apply: Keep the writing canvas dominant; show frequent formatting on text selection.
competitive_inspiration.do_not_copy: Do not reduce specialist composition and structured-document capabilities to a basic article editor.

competitive_inspiration.inspiration: Slash commands, block discovery, block handles, duplicate/move actions, recents and search.
competitive_inspiration.apply: One searchable insertion registry shared by Insert menu and slash menu; consistent block actions.
competitive_inspiration.do_not_copy: Do not create an unrestricted block universe or noisy workspace UI.

competitive_inspiration.inspiration: Canvas/layer hierarchy, contextual property inspector, responsive breakpoints and direct manipulation.
competitive_inspiration.apply: Use for selected visual compositions and device arrangements inside bounded document blocks.
competitive_inspiration.do_not_copy: Do not turn the whole document into a freeform website canvas.

competitive_inspiration.inspiration: Structured content, component properties and rich content fields.
competitive_inspiration.apply: Use typed block schemas and per-instance properties.
competitive_inspiration.do_not_copy: Do not introduce website-builder controls or CMS collection complexity into authoring.

competitive_inspiration.inspiration: Block toolbar, insertion, move/drag, block settings inspector.
competitive_inspiration.apply: Give every block clear contextual actions and independent settings.
competitive_inspiration.do_not_copy: Do not clone the full Gutenberg ecosystem or settings complexity.

competitive_inspiration.inspiration: Card-based insertion for rich media, embeds, code and callouts.
competitive_inspiration.apply: Make rich content cards first-class insertable blocks.
competitive_inspiration.do_not_copy: Do not make publishing/newsletter workflows central to this private document product.

competitive_inspiration.inspiration: Schema-driven structured content and custom object blocks.
competitive_inspiration.apply: Make templates and blocks data-driven, versioned and renderer-independent.
competitive_inspiration.do_not_copy: Do not expose developer-oriented schema configuration to ordinary users.

competitive_inspiration.inspiration: Selection, alignment, distribution, arrange/layer, grouping and keyboard operations.
competitive_inspiration.apply: Apply within visual composition blocks such as device layouts and annotated screens.
competitive_inspiration.do_not_copy: Do not add page-wide slide canvas behaviour to normal writing.

competitive_inspiration.inspiration: Case-study-specific prompts, portfolio storytelling patterns, wireframes, flows and mockup guidance.
competitive_inspiration.apply: Retain and improve the UX case-study template while making guidance reusable by other verticals.
competitive_inspiration.do_not_copy: Do not limit the overall product to UX portfolios.

competitive_inspiration.inspiration: Composable extensions, schema-driven nodes, commands, menus and NodeViews.
competitive_inspiration.apply: Keep Tiptap as the universal editing engine; implement modular extensions and shared registries.
competitive_inspiration.do_not_copy: Do not add extensions without a user workflow, persistence schema and renderer support.

template_catalog.name: UX / Product Design Case Study
template_catalog.purpose: Explain a design or product project through context, problem, role, exploration, decisions, experience and evidence-based outcomes.

sections.title: Overview
sections.purpose: Introduce the project, product, audience and the work being documented.
prompts: What product or experience did you work on?
What was your role and the project timeline?
completion_criteria: The reader understands what the project was and the author’s contribution.

sections.title: The Context
sections.purpose: Explain the circumstances that led to the project.
prompts: What was happening before the project?
What business, user or technical context mattered?

sections.title: The Challenge
sections.purpose: Define the user or business problem and why it mattered.
prompts: What problem needed to be solved?

sections.title: My Contribution
sections.purpose: Make the author’s actual responsibilities and decisions clear.

sections.title: Exploration
sections.purpose: Show how alternatives, research or design directions were explored.
prompts: Which directions were discarded and why?

sections.title: Key Decisions
sections.purpose: Explain the important choices and trade-offs.
prompts: What major decisions shaped the solution?

sections.title: The Experience
sections.purpose: Present the final product or experience and explain how it works.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.purpose: Explain the outcome using honest, attributable evidence.

sections.title: Reflection
sections.purpose: Capture learnings, limitations and what would happen next.

validation_rules: Require a meaningful title.
Do not require quantitative metrics when none exist; allow qualitative outcomes and explicit limitations.
Prompt the author to distinguish personal contribution from team contribution.
Flag unsupported numerical outcome claims for review rather than inventing evidence.
migration_notes: Preserve existing UX case-study documents and Tiptap JSON.
Map legacy sections to stable section keys only through a tested, reversible migration.
Do not delete or rewrite existing visual block attributes.

template_catalog.name: Developer Documentation
template_catalog.purpose: Create clear, task-oriented technical documentation for a product, library, SDK, API, integration or system.

sections.title: Overview
sections.purpose: Explain what the technology or system is, who it is for and when to use it.
prompts: What is this system or library?

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.purpose: List knowledge, accounts, permissions, software and versions needed before starting.
prompts: Which permissions or credentials are required?

sections.title: Quick Start
sections.purpose: Provide the shortest verified path to a working result.
prompts: What is the minimum working example?
What should the reader see after completing it?

sections.title: Installation and Setup
sections.purpose: Describe installation, environment configuration and initial setup.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.purpose: Explain domain terms and mental models before deeper implementation.
prompts: How do the main components relate?

sections.title: Implementation Guide
sections.purpose: Provide ordered, reproducible implementation instructions.
prompts: What should happen at each step?

sections.title: Code Examples
sections.purpose: Show useful, minimal, realistic examples with language and expected behaviour.
prompts: What input and output should readers expect?

sections.title: Configuration
sections.purpose: Document settings, environment variables, defaults and constraints.
prompts: What are their types and defaults?

sections.title: API / Interface Reference
sections.purpose: Describe endpoints, methods, parameters, authentication and response contracts.
prompts: What inputs and outputs are valid?
notes: Optional for guides that do not expose APIs.

sections.title: Error Handling
sections.purpose: Explain error types, recovery behaviour and safe failure handling.
prompts: What should a client do next?

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.purpose: Help readers diagnose common symptoms and resolve issues.

sections.title: Additional Resources
sections.purpose: Point to maintained references, examples and related guides.

validation_rules: Code examples must declare a language where syntax highlighting is expected.
Commands and expected output must be distinguishable.
API endpoints must validate method, path and parameter structure.
Version compatibility must be explicit when relevant.
Do not treat a code sample as executed or verified unless an execution system actually verifies it.
External links must use safe URL schemes.

template_catalog.name: Feature Specification
template_catalog.purpose: Describe the intended behaviour, scope, requirements and acceptance criteria for a specific feature before or during implementation.

sections.title: Feature Overview
sections.purpose: Summarise the proposed feature and intended value.

sections.title: Background and Context
sections.purpose: Explain the current state and why this work is being considered.

sections.title: Problem Statement
sections.purpose: State the user or business problem without jumping prematurely to a solution.
prompts: What are they trying to do?

sections.title: Objectives and Non-goals
sections.purpose: Define measurable aims and explicitly excluded scope.
prompts: What is deliberately not being solved?

sections.title: Scope and Use Cases
sections.purpose: Define included workflows, user groups and scenarios.
prompts: Which use cases are in scope?
Which scenarios are out of scope?

sections.title: Target Users and Personas
sections.purpose: Describe relevant user types and their needs without unnecessary persona theatre.
prompts: What are their needs and constraints?

sections.title: User Stories
sections.purpose: Express user intent and expected value.
prompts: As a [user], what do I need to do and why?

sections.title: Functional Requirements
sections.purpose: Define observable system behaviours with stable IDs and priorities.
prompts: What inputs, outputs and states matter?

sections.title: UX and User Flow
sections.purpose: Explain the expected interaction and important states.
prompts: What are empty, loading, success and error states?

sections.title: Edge Cases and Exceptions
sections.purpose: Document unusual, failure and boundary conditions.

sections.title: Acceptance Criteria
sections.purpose: Define testable Given/When/Then or equivalent criteria.
prompts: How can QA verify each requirement?

sections.title: Dependencies and Integrations
sections.purpose: Identify other systems, teams, APIs and prerequisites.
prompts: Which teams or services are involved?

sections.title: Success Metrics
sections.purpose: Define how the feature outcome will be evaluated.
prompts: What is the baseline and measurement window?

sections.title: Risks and Open Questions
sections.purpose: Record assumptions, unresolved questions and risks.

validation_rules: Requirement IDs must be unique within the document.
Acceptance criteria must be testable and linked to a requirement where applicable.
Separate goals from non-goals.
Do not mark assumptions as confirmed facts.
Support Must/Should/Could/Won’t priority labels without forcing every requirement to have a priority.

template_catalog.name: Release Notes and Changelog
template_catalog.purpose: Communicate product changes for a specific release in a clear, useful and audience-appropriate way.

sections.title: Release Header
sections.purpose: Identify product, version, release date and audience.
prompts: What product and version is this?

sections.title: Release Overview
sections.purpose: Summarise the most important changes.
prompts: What is most important in this release?

sections.title: New Features
sections.purpose: Describe newly available capabilities and their user value.

sections.title: Improvements
sections.purpose: Describe enhancements to existing functionality.

sections.title: Bug Fixes
sections.purpose: Describe resolved issues at an appropriate detail level.

sections.title: Breaking Changes
sections.purpose: Clearly identify incompatible changes and affected users.

sections.title: Migration Instructions
sections.purpose: Give safe, ordered upgrade instructions when needed.
prompts: How can the change be verified?

sections.title: Deprecations
sections.purpose: Explain features being deprecated and timelines.

sections.title: Known Issues
sections.purpose: Disclose known limitations and available workarounds.

sections.title: Compatibility
sections.purpose: State supported versions, platforms and dependencies.

sections.title: Resources
sections.purpose: Link to documentation, support and related announcements.

validation_rules: Version and release date must be explicit.
Breaking changes must include impact and required action.
Migration instructions must not be hidden in general prose.
Do not imply a feature is available if status is planned or unreleased.
Allow multiple release channels and audience-specific tone.

template_catalog.name: Marketing Case Study
template_catalog.purpose: Tell an evidence-based customer or campaign success story that explains context, strategy, execution and measurable outcomes.

sections.title: Hero and Client Introduction
sections.purpose: Introduce the client, project and central result without exaggeration.
prompts: What is the clearest supported outcome?

sections.title: Client Background
sections.purpose: Explain the customer, market and starting context.

sections.title: The Challenge
sections.purpose: Describe the business or customer problem.

sections.title: Objectives
sections.purpose: State the agreed business and campaign objectives.

sections.title: Strategy
sections.purpose: Explain the approach and rationale.

sections.title: Execution
sections.purpose: Describe the work delivered and the sequence of activities.
prompts: Which channels or assets were used?

sections.title: Solution Delivered
sections.purpose: Show the final deliverables and how they addressed the challenge.

sections.title: Results and Impact
sections.purpose: Communicate supported outcomes with context and attribution.

sections.title: Customer Testimonial
sections.purpose: Include approved customer feedback and exact attribution.
prompts: Is there an approved customer quote?
Who said it and in what capacity?

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.purpose: Summarise lessons and transferable insights.
prompts: What would be repeated or changed?

sections.title: Next Steps and Call to Action
sections.purpose: Provide a useful next action without turning the document into an unsupported sales claim.
prompts: What should interested readers do next?

validation_rules: Metric claims must support baseline, measurement period and source where available.
Clearly distinguish measured results from estimates or projections.
Require permission/consent metadata before using identifiable client names, logos or testimonials in public-facing exports.
Do not fabricate quotes, logos, customer identities or outcome data.
Allow an honest qualitative outcome when quantitative data is unavailable.

sections.title: Background and Opportunity
sections.purpose: Explain the product context and opportunity.

sections.title: Problem Statement
sections.purpose: Define the problem and affected users.

sections.title: Target Users and Needs
sections.purpose: Describe target segments and their needs.

sections.title: Goals and Non-goals
sections.purpose: Set intended outcomes and explicit exclusions.
prompts: What is not part of this initiative?

sections.title: Proposed Solution
sections.purpose: Describe the intended product direction.

sections.title: User Journeys
sections.purpose: Show the major journeys and states.

sections.title: Requirements

prompts: What qualities or constraints must it meet?

sections.title: Success Metrics
sections.purpose: Define outcome measures, baseline and target where known.

sections.title: Dependencies
sections.purpose: Describe teams, systems, decisions and external dependencies.

sections.title: Risks and Assumptions
sections.purpose: Capture uncertainty and mitigation.

sections.title: Rollout and Launch
sections.purpose: Describe rollout, communication and adoption considerations.

sections.title: Open Questions and Decisions
sections.purpose: Track unresolved topics and owners.

validation_rules: Separate problem, goals, solution and requirements.
Allow unknown targets to remain explicitly unknown.
Requirements should be traceable and testable where possible.
Risk entries should support owner and mitigation fields.

sections.title: Problem Context
sections.purpose: Explain the current system and the need for change.

sections.title: Goals and Non-goals

sections.title: Process Overview
sections.purpose: Show the process at a glance.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Procedure
sections.purpose: Describe actionable steps in execution order.

sections.title: Decision Points
sections.purpose: Explain branches and criteria for decisions.

sections.purpose: Explain failures, exceptions, escalation triggers and ownership.

sections.title: Quality Checklist

sections.title: Service Levels and Timelines

sections.title: Related Documents

validation_rules: Procedure steps must have a meaningful sequence.
Responsibilities must be clear for critical actions.
Exceptions and escalations must identify the next action or owner where known.
Review/effective dates must not be fabricated.
Support version and revision history.

architecture.principle: The editor is universal; templates and block registries configure the creation experience.

layers.name: Universal editor engine
layers.responsibility: Tiptap document editing, selection, history, keyboard shortcuts, autosave integration and responsive canvas.

layers.name: Template engine
layers.responsibility: Document type, category, section structure, prompts, metadata fields, evidence guidance, block recommendations, validation and export profile.

layers.name: Block registry
layers.responsibility: Canonical block schemas, insertion commands, toolbar actions, inspectors, renderers, validation, accessibility and migrations.

layers.name: Guidance engine
layers.responsibility: Contextual section prompts, evidence reminders, recommended visuals and completion criteria. Guidance remains separate from document content.

layers.name: Review engine
layers.responsibility: Template-aware structural and content-presence checks. Does not claim objective writing quality.

layers.name: Rendering/export engine
layers.responsibility: Authenticated preview and output profiles using shared renderers and safe fallbacks.

proposed_routes.auth: authenticated or public read only if product permits; no user data

dashboard.empty_state: Explain the creation workflow and offer Create Document. Do not show a blank dashboard.

creation_flow: Choose a category or search all templates.
Choose a template, blank document or duplicate one of the user’s own documents.
Review template purpose, audience, sections, blocks and output options.
Enter required and optional metadata; allow optional fields to be skipped.
Preview and customise the generated outline.
Optionally select private assets from the user’s own media library.
Create a private draft and open the universal editor.

editor_layout.left: Story Outline: sections, order, status, add/rename/duplicate/delete and navigation.
editor_layout.center: Writing Canvas: Tiptap content, inline formatting, block insertion and responsive document flow.
editor_layout.right: Contextual panel: Guidance by default; Properties for selected blocks; Media when asset selection is invoked.
responsive: Desktop: three regions; collapse panels as needed.
Tablet: central canvas prioritised with drawer/panel access.
Mobile: single-column editing and reading; complex composition controls may be limited.

architecture.content_source_of_truth: Versioned Tiptap JSON plus document metadata. Do not create separate unsynchronised outline content; section identity and order must be represented consistently in the document model or a transactionally maintained structure.

data_model.instruction: First inspect current live tables. The following is a logical target model, not permission to blindly create duplicate tables. Adapt names and migrations to the current schema.

entities.name: studio_documents
constraints: workspace_id references the owner’s personal workspace
status uses an explicit allowed set
Indexes on owner_id, workspace_id, document_type, template_id and updated_at
entities.privacy: RLS allows only authenticated owner access; workspace-owner relationship must be verified.

entities.name: studio_document_versions
entities.purpose: Future version history; implement only if current product roadmap includes it in this cycle

entities.name: studio_assets
entities.privacy: RLS on metadata and independent Storage RLS on object access.

entities.name: system_template_definitions
entities.purpose: Conceptual application-configured system templates; initially maintained in version-controlled code/config rather than a mutable user table

entities.name: user_templates
entities.purpose: Future user-owned custom templates; do not implement unless explicitly prioritised

migration_requirements: Back up staging/production data before migration.
Preserve existing document IDs wherever possible.
Preserve owner_id, workspace_id and asset references.
Verify document counts and content checksums/structural equivalence.
Do not drop old tables until migration, application cutover, rollback window and QA are complete.
Do not change the established authentication or workspace model.

rules: Template IDs are stable and unique.
Section keys are stable and unique within a template version.
Template versions are immutable after release.
Every template has at least one meaningful section.
Every suggested block must exist in the block registry or be explicitly marked future.
Required sections are explicit; optional sections do not block completion.
Template data is validated at build/test time.
Existing documents remain pinned to their original template version.
Template upgrade is explicit and shows a before/after outline and content impact.

shared_behaviours: Same insert command works from toolbar, slash menu and contextual recommendations.
Block handles support appropriate drag, duplicate, delete, insert before/after and move actions.
Block schema and renderers are versioned.
All visual blocks have responsive fallbacks.
All data visualisations provide textual or tabular alternatives.

universal_toolbar_groups.visibility: Text selection; compact bubble menu for frequent actions
Always available through compact action and slash menu

selection_behaviour: Preserve editor selection when toolbar buttons are clicked.
Only show commands supported by current selection.
Disabled actions must have a reason when useful.
Provide keyboard equivalents for essential operations.
contextual_recommendations: Use current document_type, template_id, section_key and user recent/frequent blocks to rank insertion suggestions.
Suggestions never restrict access to universal compatible blocks.
Do not collect document text to make recommendations unless a separately consented feature is introduced.
competitor_pattern_adoption: Notion: slash menu, search, block handles and recents.
WordPress Gutenberg: block toolbar plus inspector.
Framer/Webflow: contextual properties and responsive composition settings.
Google Slides: align, distribute, arrange and group within bounded visual composition blocks.
Tiptap: composable extensions and node views.

guidance_rules: Prompts are not inserted into authored content.
Author can ignore, edit or remove any suggested section.
Private author notes are not exported by default.
Guidance must not claim that missing information exists.
review_dimensions: Missing alt text for informative images
guidance_and_review.review_scoring_policy: Do not create a simplistic universal quality score. Show transparent completion and validation signals. Writing quality judgements, if introduced later, must be explainable and optional.

requirements: Explicit fallbacks for unsupported visual blocks
Asset manifest with private storage paths or export-local asset references

privacy_and_security_invariants: All documents remain private by default. No public publishing, public sharing links or public document directory is introduced in this scope.
Both existing account authentication methods remain supported: email/password and email OTP, with verified email as required by the established account policy.
One personal workspace per user remains the current workspace model.
Every document and private asset remains linked to authenticated owner_id and workspace_id.
Never trust owner_id or workspace_id supplied by the client; derive and validate them server-side from the authenticated session.
RLS remains enabled and enforced for all document, asset, custom-template and version records that are user-owned.
Private Storage remains private. Storage object policies independently verify workspace/document ownership.
Preview and export operations must be authenticated and owner-authorized. Do not use shared public caches for private content.
Signed URLs, if used, must be short-lived and generated only after ownership verification. Do not persist signed URLs in document JSON.
Do not expose Supabase service-role keys or privileged credentials to the browser. Privileged operations require explicit server authorization.
Analytics must never contain document body text, private notes, uploaded media, signed URLs, secrets or sensitive identifiers.
Code blocks are content, not executable code. Never execute user-submitted code or render unsanitized HTML.
External embeds must use an allowlist, safe URL validation, sandboxing and appropriate privacy controls.
Diagram source must be sanitised. Do not inject unsanitised SVG/HTML from user content.
Template definitions distributed by the application are read-only system assets. User-created templates, if added later, must be owner-scoped.
No document is made public merely because it is exported or marked ready_for_review.

implementation_phases.name: Repository, product and data audit
implementation_phases.execution_gate: Do not change schema or UI until the current implementation is mapped.
implementation_phases.objective: Establish the current live implementation and identify exactly what can be reused for multi-vertical documents.
implementation_phases.why: Earlier source ZIPs may not represent the current six-phase multi-user implementation. The live repository is the only source of truth.

actions.action: Inspect all current dashboard, document creation, editor, preview, review, export, media and settings routes.
actions.why: Determine where document-specific assumptions are embedded.
evaluate: Every relevant route is listed with auth requirements.
No old route is assumed to exist without verification.

actions.action: Inspect current Supabase schema, migrations, document tables, owner/workspace relationships, RLS, storage buckets and indexes.
actions.why: Generalisation must preserve the completed privacy architecture.
evaluate: All user-owned tables and storage policies are identified.
Existing UX documents and media ownership are understood.

actions.action: Inspect Tiptap extensions, node schemas, toolbar, slash menu, block inspector, insert registry, node views, validation, autosave, renderer and export code.
actions.why: Reuse working editor infrastructure and avoid duplicating extensions.
actions.deliverable: Editor capability inventory and dependency map.
evaluate: Every existing block is catalogued.
Each block is mapped to editor, persistence, preview and export support.

actions.action: Inspect the current UX case-study framework and its stored document JSON.
actions.why: Existing UX case studies must survive generalisation unchanged.
evaluate: Existing headings, section data and visual blocks are mapped.
Migration approach is reversible and testable.

actions.action: Run current build, lint, typecheck, unit tests, integration tests and representative UX document flows.
actions.why: Establish a regression baseline before changes.
evaluate: Known failures are recorded before implementation.
Baseline screenshots or fixtures exist for important flows.

exit_criteria: Current repository version and architecture are confirmed.
Existing UX case-study workflow can be reproduced.
No unresolved critical uncertainty about ownership or storage.

implementation_phases.name: Generalise the document model
implementation_phases.execution_gate: Data model and migration design must be reviewed before applying production migrations.
implementation_phases.objective: Evolve from a case-study-specific entity to a generic private document entity while preserving existing documents.
implementation_phases.why: Multiple verticals should use one document engine without storing developer guides or SOPs in a semantically case-study-specific table.

actions.action: Design a generic studio_documents model with id, workspace_id, owner_id, title, description, document_type, template_id, template_version, content JSONB, metadata JSONB, document_schema_version, status, created_at and updated_at. Adjust field names to existing conventions.
actions.why: Separate document identity from template-specific content.
actions.deliverable: Reviewed ERD and TypeScript data contract.
evaluate: Every new document has stable ownership and workspace references.
document_type and template references are explicit.
Content JSON remains the source of truth for editor content.

actions.action: Define private lifecycle states such as draft, in_progress, ready_for_review and archived. Keep completion/review state distinct from public publishing.
actions.why: Different document types need review states without implying public publication.
evaluate: No public or published status is introduced for this release.
Invalid state transitions are rejected.

actions.action: Create an additive, versioned, reversible migration from the current case-study-specific model to generic documents. Preserve IDs, workspace_id, owner_id, content JSON, timestamps, metadata and asset references.
actions.why: Avoid losing user work or breaking existing editor references.
actions.deliverable: Migration SQL, backfill script, verification query and rollback procedure.
evaluate: Record counts match before and after.
Owner/workspace relations are unchanged.
JSON hashes or structural comparisons prove content preservation.
Rollback is tested in staging.

actions.action: Add template_id and template_version to document records. Keep system template definitions version-controlled in application code/config for the initial release.
actions.why: A document must retain the template version it started with even when templates evolve.
evaluate: Existing documents can point to the legacy UX template version.
Updating a template does not silently alter existing documents.

actions.action: Create generic document queries and mutations with owner/workspace scoping. Remove case-study-specific naming from new shared abstractions where appropriate.
actions.why: The dashboard, editor and export pipeline need one document repository.
evaluate: All CRUD operations are authenticated and owner-scoped.
No client-supplied owner_id is trusted.

exit_criteria: Existing UX documents are preserved.
RLS remains effective on the generic document entity.
All CRUD operations work for two separate test accounts.
No unauthorised public read path exists.

implementation_phases.name: Template engine and library
implementation_phases.execution_gate: Template schema must be approved before building all template content.
implementation_phases.objective: Make document structures configurable, versioned and independent from editor components.
implementation_phases.why: New verticals should be introduced by adding template definitions rather than building separate editors.

actions.action: Implement a versioned template contract with id, version, name, category, description, audience, purpose, metadata fields, sections, prompts, writing guidance, suggested evidence, suggested blocks, completion criteria, validation rules and export profiles.
actions.why: Standardise how every template describes its creation workflow.
evaluate: Invalid template definitions fail validation.
Stable section keys are unique within a template.
Required and optional sections are explicit.

actions.action: Build a registry for loading, listing, previewing and resolving templates by ID and version.
actions.why: The project wizard, editor guidance and review system must share the same definitions.
evaluate: All UI surfaces resolve the same template version.
Missing template references fail gracefully.

actions.action: Make published system template versions immutable. New revisions create a new version. Existing documents remain pinned unless the user explicitly chooses a migration.
actions.why: Prevent silent content and structure changes.
actions.deliverable: Version compatibility policy and migration UX.
evaluate: Existing documents retain their template version.
Explicit template upgrade previews changes before applying them.

actions.action: Build document category and template discovery UI with search, descriptions, audience, section preview, recommended blocks and output formats.
actions.why: Users must understand which starting point fits their job.
evaluate: User can locate a template by category or search.
Template preview accurately represents its generated outline.

actions.action: Build Create Document flow: choose category, choose template or blank, enter optional metadata, customise outline, create private draft.
actions.why: Reduce blank-page friction while retaining user freedom.
evaluate: All optional fields can be skipped.
Back/continue preserves entered values.
The resulting document uses the selected template version and is private.

exit_criteria: A new template can be added through configuration without creating a new editor.
Blank documents are supported.
Existing UX template remains selectable and compatible.

implementation_phases.name: Universal block registry and editor adaptation
implementation_phases.execution_gate: Block contract and renderer compatibility must be agreed before adding many new blocks.
implementation_phases.objective: Create one extensible block system for writing, media, data, visual composition and structured domain content.
implementation_phases.why: Every template should reuse canonical blocks, while each block remains editable, validated, accessible and exportable.

actions.action: Define block metadata: id, version, category, label, description, search terms, supported document types, schema, insertion command, capabilities, toolbar actions, inspector, editor renderer, preview renderer, export renderer, validation and migration.
actions.why: Prevent one-off implementations and inconsistent behaviour.
evaluate: Every registered block has editor and output behaviour.
Block schemas are versioned.
Unsupported block types produce safe fallback handling.

actions.action: Build a shared insertion registry powering the top Insert menu, slash menu, inline plus menu and section recommendations.
actions.why: Avoid separate lists and divergent insertion behaviour.
evaluate: Each block appears consistently across supported insertion surfaces.
Search supports labels and synonyms.
Recent/frequent items do not bypass permission or compatibility rules.

actions.action: Standardise block actions: select, drag, duplicate, delete, insert before/after, move, convert where compatible and open inspector.
actions.why: Adopt predictable Notion/Gutenberg-style block management.
actions.deliverable: Reusable block handle and contextual menu.
evaluate: Keyboard users can perform equivalent actions.
Selection remains stable after menu interaction.
Undo/redo covers block operations.

actions.action: Register existing UX visual blocks as canonical block definitions without changing their meaning or stored attributes.
actions.why: Preserve the working UX case-study experience.
actions.deliverable: Existing block registry entries and regression fixtures.
evaluate: All old documents render identically within agreed tolerances.
No block loses data after save/reopen/export.

actions.action: Prioritise reusable code block, terminal, parameter table, process timeline, flow diagram, requirement list, user story, acceptance criteria, testimonial, procedure steps, checklist and reference list.
actions.why: These cover the first new verticals with reusable primitives.
evaluate: Each block supports keyboard, responsive and export behaviour.
No block stores executable or unsafe arbitrary markup.

exit_criteria: A new block can be registered once and used by multiple templates.
All blocks round-trip through save and reload.
Private asset references remain owner-scoped.

implementation_phases.name: Release 1 templates: developer docs, feature specs, release notes and marketing case studies
implementation_phases.execution_gate: Do not mark a template complete until a domain reviewer can create a usable real document with it.
implementation_phases.objective: Ship the first four new vertical templates while retaining UX Case Study.
implementation_phases.why: These templates test technical, product, release communication and marketing storytelling needs using the shared architecture.

actions.action: Implement the Developer Documentation v1 definition and essential code/terminal/API/parameter/technical-callout blocks. Include optional API/reference and troubleshooting sections.
actions.why: Support engineers and technical writers.
actions.deliverable: Developer Documentation template and sample document.
evaluate: Engineer can create a getting-started/integration guide.
Code language, command and output remain distinguishable.
API fields and parameter tables are structured.
Code is escaped and never executed during rendering.

actions.action: Implement Feature Specification v1 with requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, edge cases, dependencies, success metrics and risks.
actions.why: Support product-to-engineering handoff.
actions.deliverable: Feature Specification template and sample document.
evaluate: Requirement IDs are stable and unique.
Acceptance scenarios are testable.
Scope, non-scope and open questions are distinguishable.

actions.action: Implement Release Notes v1 with version header, summary, features, improvements, fixes, breaking changes, migrations, deprecations, known issues and compatibility.
actions.why: Support product and engineering release communication.
actions.deliverable: Release Notes template and sample document.
evaluate: Version/date are explicit.
Breaking changes include impact and action.
Planned work is not represented as released.

actions.action: Implement Marketing Case Study v1 with customer context, challenge, objectives, strategy, execution, solution, results, testimonials, takeaways and CTA.
actions.why: Support agencies, marketing teams and customer success.
actions.deliverable: Marketing Case Study template and sample document.
evaluate: Results support baseline, period and source where available.
Testimonial attribution and permission are explicit.
Estimated and measured outcomes are distinguished.

actions.action: Retain and improve the existing UX Case Study as a first-class template on the generic document engine.
actions.why: Multi-vertical expansion must not regress the original use case.
actions.deliverable: UX template compatibility and regression report.
evaluate: Existing documents open, edit, preview and export.
Existing section content and block data are preserved.

expected_deliverables: One realistic sample document per template
exit_criteria: Five document types work on the same editor and persistence engine.
Each new template has at least one domain-reviewed sample.
No cross-template data or permission leakage.

implementation_phases.name: Release 2 templates: PRD, technical design, ADR and SOP
implementation_phases.execution_gate: Only begin after Release 1 templates pass functional and domain-quality evaluation.
implementation_phases.objective: Expand into product strategy, architecture and operations documentation.
implementation_phases.why: These use cases broaden the audience while reusing the same template and block foundation.

actions.action: Implement PRD template with opportunity, problem, users, goals/non-goals, solution, journeys, requirements, success metrics, dependencies, risks, rollout and open questions.
actions.why: Support product managers and founders.
evaluate: Goals are separated from requirements.
Assumptions and risks are explicit.
Metrics support baseline/target/source metadata when known.

actions.action: Implement Technical Design Document with current state, goals, constraints, proposed architecture, components, data model, interfaces, data flow, security, performance, failure modes, testing, alternatives and deployment.
actions.why: Support engineering design review and technical alignment.
evaluate: Current and proposed architecture are distinguishable.
Security, failure handling and testing are represented.
Alternatives and trade-offs are recorded.

actions.action: Implement a compact Architecture Decision Record companion template with status, context, decision drivers, options, decision, consequences and references.
actions.why: Capture one significant technical decision without requiring a full design document.
evaluate: Decision status is explicit.
Alternatives and consequences are captured.
Accepted records are not silently overwritten.

actions.action: Implement SOP/Process Playbook with document info, purpose, scope, roles, prerequisites, overview, steps, decisions, exceptions/escalations, quality, SLA, references and revision history.
actions.why: Support repeatable operational knowledge.
evaluate: Steps are executable and ordered.
Responsibilities and escalation paths are clear.
Printable checklist and revision history work.

exit_criteria: All templates pass their domain-specific evaluation.
No new template requires a separate editor implementation.

implementation_phases.name: Template-aware review and output
implementation_phases.execution_gate: Output profiles must not weaken document privacy or expose private assets.
implementation_phases.objective: Make different document types reviewable and portable through suitable outputs.
implementation_phases.why: Users need useful deliverables outside the editor; different documents require different rendering conventions.

actions.action: Build template-aware review checks using required sections, completion criteria, block validation and missing evidence prompts.
actions.why: Help users identify incomplete or inconsistent documentation.
evaluate: Warnings link to the relevant section or block.
No arbitrary quality score is presented as objective truth.
Optional sections do not block completion.

actions.action: Use one canonical rendering system for authenticated preview and export, with document-type-specific presentation profiles.
actions.why: Prevent preview/export drift.
evaluate: Editor content, preview and export preserve semantic structure.
All supported blocks have a fallback renderer.

actions.action: Implement PDF output profiles for editorial, technical, product and SOP documents.
actions.why: Different documents need appropriate pagination and layout.
evaluate: No clipped content or broken page breaks.
Code blocks remain readable.
Tables and diagrams do not overflow.
Generated file is downloadable only by the owner.

actions.action: Implement standalone responsive HTML ZIP export with local assets and no dependency on expiring signed URLs.
actions.why: Enable portable reading and hosting elsewhere.
evaluate: ZIP works offline or from extracted local files.
All referenced assets are included or clearly reported.
No private app session is required to view the exported copy.

actions.action: Implement Markdown export with explicit unsupported-block fallbacks and JSON plus asset manifest backup.
actions.why: Provide content portability and full-fidelity backup.
evaluate: Text order and headings are preserved.
Unsupported visuals have meaningful fallback descriptions.
Backup can be validated against the document schema.

exit_criteria: Exports are correct, portable and owner-authorized.
No public document publishing or sharing is introduced.

implementation_phases.name: Cross-vertical QA, beta validation and iteration
implementation_phases.execution_gate: No public launch with unresolved critical security or data integrity defects.
implementation_phases.objective: Validate the quality and usefulness of each template with people who actually create that kind of document.
implementation_phases.why: A technically valid template can still be structurally wrong or unhelpful to its intended audience.

actions.action: Run unit, integration, end-to-end, accessibility, responsive, migration, export and security tests.
actions.why: Verify the shared system and all vertical configurations.
evaluate: All critical tests pass.
No P0/P1 security or data integrity defects remain.

actions.action: Have 2–3 relevant practitioners review each new template structure and sample output as an initial qualitative check.
actions.why: Validate domain completeness and usefulness.
evaluate: Reviewers can complete a realistic document.
Missing and redundant sections are documented.
Template is revised based on evidence.

actions.action: Run moderated or observed tests with a small cross-vertical beta cohort; recruit users from engineering, product, marketing and operations.
actions.why: Find creation friction and prove the workflow.
actions.deliverable: Task completion observations, feedback and funnel report.
evaluate: Users can select the right template.
Users can create, edit, preview and export.
Abandonment reasons are categorised.

actions.action: Instrument privacy-safe events for template selection, document creation, block insertion, review, export and return usage.
actions.why: Measure real adoption and repeat value.
evaluate: No document text, private notes or asset contents are collected.
Events are documented and testable.

actions.action: Prioritise fixes based on observed user behaviour and domain reviews.
actions.why: Avoid speculative feature expansion.
evaluate: Every roadmap item is linked to observed friction or validated user need.

exit_criteria: All critical privacy tests pass.
Each new template has domain review evidence.
No blocking export or data-loss defects remain.
Known limitations are documented.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: A new user opens Create Document and browses categories.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: The user can identify category, audience, purpose and template structure before selecting it.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: User creates one document from each Release 1 template.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: Correct document_type, template_id and template_version are stored, with generated sections and private ownership.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: User starts from blank.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: A valid generic document is created and can accept universal blocks.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: A template definition is updated after a document has been created.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: Existing document remains pinned to its original version until an explicit upgrade.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: User adds, renames, duplicates, reorders and deletes sections.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: Stable section IDs, content and order persist correctly.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: User opens guidance, adds a private note and exports the document.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: Guidance and private notes are excluded unless explicitly authored as document content.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: A block is inserted from toolbar, slash menu and section recommendations.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: All surfaces use the same schema and insertion command.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: Existing UX case study is opened, edited and exported after migration.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: All text, formatting, assets and visual blocks are preserved.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: User creates a guide with installation commands, code samples and API parameters.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: Code, commands, output, endpoints and parameter data remain structured and readable.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: User creates requirements and acceptance criteria.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: Requirement IDs remain unique and scenarios are testable.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: User documents a release with breaking changes and migration steps.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: Version/date, impact and actions are clear; unreleased items are not presented as released.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: User documents customer results and testimonial.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: Metric source, baseline and period can be recorded; testimonial consent/attribution is explicit.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: User documents proposed architecture and trade-offs.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: Current/proposed states, security, failure handling, testing and alternatives are distinguishable.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: User creates a procedure with steps, roles and escalation path.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: Procedure is ordered, printable and operationally actionable.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: User B guesses User A document ID and queries API.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: No document data is returned and mutation is denied by RLS.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: User B requests User A private asset.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: Download is denied; no public URL exposes the file.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: User B attempts to export User A document.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: Export generation and download are denied.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: Export technical, marketing, product and SOP examples.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: No clipped content, broken code blocks, missing assets or unreadable tables.
acceptance_test_matrix.evidence: Visual PDF inspection and automated checks.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: Extract the HTML ZIP and open it outside the application.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: Local assets load, responsive layout works and no temporary signed URL is required.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: Export Markdown and JSON backup.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: Structure and text are preserved; unsupported blocks have explicit fallbacks; asset manifest is complete.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: Inspect emitted event payloads.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: No document body, private notes, asset content or secret URLs are sent.

acceptance_test_matrix.scenario: Complete creation and editing using keyboard and screen reader semantics.
acceptance_test_matrix.expected: Controls have accessible labels, visible focus, logical order and appropriate semantics.

scoring_scale.3: Meets acceptance criteria with test evidence

quality_dimensions.evaluation: Every required action works across template creation, editor, blocks, preview and export.
Sections and guidance are relevant, complete and reviewed by practitioners from the intended domain.
Users can find the right template, understand prompts and use editor controls without avoidable confusion.
Content survives save, reload, migration, preview and export without loss or structural corruption.
All cross-account database, storage, preview and export tests deny access. Any critical privacy failure is an automatic release blocker regardless of score.
Keyboard, focus, semantics, contrast, mobile and tablet behaviours are acceptable.
New template or block can be added without creating a separate editor or duplicating core logic.

mandatory_conditions: No unresolved P0 or P1 data-loss defects.
No unresolved P0 or P1 cross-account access defects.
All Release 1 templates have at least one realistic sample document.
All blocks used by a template work in editor, preview and relevant exports.
Migration and rollback have been tested in staging.
Build, typecheck and lint pass; known exceptions documented.

evidence_required: Screenshots or screen recordings of core flows

analytics_specification.north_star_metric: Completed documents per active creator, segmented by document_type and template.
analytics_specification.activation_candidate: A user creates a document, adds meaningful content in at least three relevant sections, inserts at least one relevant block where appropriate, and opens private preview. Validate this definition with beta behaviour; do not enforce as a universal completion rule.

required_project_deliverables.evaluation: Complete traceability from current implementation to the target architecture.

required_project_deliverables.name: Product UX specification
required_project_deliverables.evaluation: Every core user journey has screens, states, interactions and edge cases.

required_project_deliverables.name: Document data architecture
required_project_deliverables.evaluation: No data loss; all ownership checks preserved.

required_project_deliverables.name: Template library
required_project_deliverables.evaluation: Every template passes its structure and domain review.

required_project_deliverables.name: Block registry
required_project_deliverables.evaluation: Every registered block works across the required lifecycle.

required_project_deliverables.name: Operational documentation
required_project_deliverables.evaluation: Another engineer can add a template or block using documented steps.

release_plan.release_1: Keep existing UX Case Study and add Developer Documentation, Feature Specification, Release Notes and Marketing Case Study. This is the first multi-vertical release.
release_plan.release_2: Add Product Requirements Document, Technical Design Document, ADR companion template and SOP / Process Playbook.
release_plan.later: Add specialisations such as API reference, Getting Started, integration guide, campaign performance report, research report, postmortem and knowledge-base article based on user demand.
release_plan.release_rule: Do not release a template solely because the outline exists. It must have contextual guidance, relevant blocks, validation, sample content, preview/export support and domain-review evidence.

future_features: AI writing and refinement with explicit consent
Template sharing if privacy model is redesigned
Import from Markdown or other document formats

release_2_companion_template.name: Architecture Decision Record (ADR)
release_2_companion_template.purpose: Capture one significant technical decision and its context, alternatives and consequences.

sections.title: Status
sections.purpose: Show proposed, accepted, rejected, superseded or deprecated status.
prompts: What is the current decision status?

sections.title: Context
sections.purpose: Explain the problem and forces influencing the decision.

sections.title: Decision Drivers
sections.purpose: List the factors used to evaluate options.

sections.title: Options Considered
sections.purpose: Record realistic options and trade-offs.

sections.title: Decision
sections.purpose: State the selected option and rationale.

sections.title: Consequences
sections.purpose: Document positive, negative and follow-up consequences.
prompts: What debt or risk is accepted?

sections.title: References
sections.purpose: Link related design documents, issues and discussions.
